AE.description: A cluster of six oases in Al Ain with traditional falaj irrigation systems that have sustained life in the desert for millennia.
AE.name: Al Ain Oasis

AR.description: The Argentine side of the world's most spectacular waterfall system, accessible via walkways into the 'Devil's Throat.'
AR.name: Iguazú National Park

AR.description: Home to Perito Moreno Glacier — one of the few advancing glaciers in the world — and the jagged Fitz Roy massif.
AR.name: Los Glaciares National Park

AR.description: A 17th-century Jesuit complex including South America's oldest university, demonstrating the Jesuits' unique rural missions.
AR.name: Jesuit Block and Estancias of Córdoba

AR.description: A key site for the conservation of marine mammals including southern right whales, elephant seals, and penguins.
AR.name: Península Valdés

AT.description: The principal summer residence of Habsburg emperors, with 1,441 rooms and magnificent Baroque gardens.
AT.name: Palace and Gardens of Schönbrunn

AT.description: Vienna's Ringstrasse boulevard features world-class museums, the State Opera, Parliament, and imperial palaces.
AT.name: Historic Centre of Vienna

AT.description: The village of Hallstatt on a Alpine lake was the center of Celtic salt mining for 3,000 years.
AT.name: Hallstatt-Dachstein / Salzkammergut Cultural Landscape

AU.description: The world's largest coral reef system (2,300 km), visible from space — home to 1,500 species of fish and 4,000 types of mollusk.
AU.name: Great Barrier Reef

AU.description: Jørn Utzon's 1973 masterpiece with its distinctive sail-shaped shells is one of the 20th century's greatest architectural works.
AU.name: Sydney Opera House

AU.description: Contains the world's largest collection of Aboriginal rock art, some over 20,000 years old, alongside diverse billabong ecosystems.
AU.name: Kakadu National Park

AU.description: The sacred red monolith Uluru (Ayers Rock) and the domed rocks of Kata Tjuta are the spiritual heart of the Anangu people.
AU.name: Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park

BD.description: An ancient mosque city built in the 15th century by the Muslim saint Khan Jahan Ali, containing 360 mosques and religious buildings.
BD.name: Mosque City of Bagerhat

BD.description: The largest known Buddhist monastery south of the Himalayas (8th century), which influenced Buddhist architecture across Asia.
BD.name: Ruins of the Buddhist Vihara at Paharpur

BD.description: The world's largest mangrove forest at the mouth of the Ganges, home to the iconic Bengal tiger and Irrawaddy dolphin.
BD.name: The Sundarbans

BE.description: The central market square of Brussels, surrounded by opulent Baroque guild halls — Victor Hugo called it 'the most beautiful square in the world.'
BE.name: Grand Place, Brussels

BE.description: 56 towers (32 in Belgium) that were powerful symbols of the growing power of medieval towns.
BE.name: Belfries of Belgium and France

BE.description: The best-preserved Renaissance printing house in the world, showing how the printing press transformed European civilization.
BE.name: Plantin-Moretus Museum, Antwerp

BR.description: The widest waterfall system in the world: 275 falls up to 82 m high and 2.7 km wide along the Brazil-Argentina border.
BR.name: Iguaçu National Park

BR.description: The modernist capital built from scratch in 41 months (1956–1960), a UNESCO city for its urban planning by Costa and Niemeyer.
BR.name: Brasília

BR.description: A former gold-rush capital of Brazil with exceptional 18th-century Baroque architecture and sculptures by Aleijadinho.
BR.name: Historic Town of Ouro Preto

BR.description: The world's largest protected area of tropical rainforest, critical for global climate regulation.
BR.name: Central Amazon Conservation Complex

CH.description: One of the finest examples of Carolingian architecture in the world, with a library housing 170,000 manuscripts dating to the 8th century.
CH.name: Convent of Saint Gall

CH.description: The largest glacier in the Alps (Aletsch Glacier, 23 km), with the iconic Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks.
CH.name: Jungfrau-Aletsch Protected Area

CH.description: A masterpiece of railway engineering crossing the Alps with 196 bridges and viaducts at up to 2,253 m elevation.
CH.name: Rhaetian Railway in the Albula/Bernina Landscapes

CL.description: The remote Pacific island with 900 monumental stone statues (moai) carved by the Polynesian Rapa Nui people from the 10th century.
CL.name: Rapa Nui National Park (Easter Island)

CL.description: Chile's 'Jewel of the Pacific': a labyrinth of hills with colorful houses, funiculars, and street murals.
CL.name: Historic Quarter of the Seaport City of Valparaíso

CL.description: Sixteen wooden churches built by the Jesuits in the 17th–18th centuries, representing a unique mestizo tradition.
CL.name: Churches of Chiloé

CN.description: Stretching over 21,000 km, it is the largest military structure ever built, constructed across centuries of Chinese history.
CN.name: The Great Wall

CN.description: The world's largest palace complex, home to 24 Chinese emperors over nearly 500 years.
CN.name: Imperial Palace of the Ming and Qing Dynasties (Forbidden City)

CN.description: The burial site of China's first emperor includes over 8,000 life-sized terracotta warriors, horses, and chariots.
CN.name: Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor (Terracotta Army)

CN.description: Contains fossils of Homo erectus pekinensis dating back 250,000–500,000 years, providing critical evidence of human evolution.
CN.name: Peking Man Site at Zhoukoudian

CN.description: The most revered of China's Five Sacred Mountains, a place of pilgrimage for 3,000 years with over 22 temples and hundreds of inscriptions.
CN.name: Mount Taishan

CN.description: The masterpiece of Chinese landscape garden design, centering on Kunming Lake and Longevity Hill.
CN.name: Summer Palace, Beijing

CN.description: Renowned for granite peaks, ancient pines, hot springs, and clouds — one of China's most famous scenic spots.
CN.name: Huangshan (Yellow Mountains)

CN.description: Known for its colorful lakes, multi-level waterfalls, and snow-capped peaks, home to the giant panda.
CN.name: Jiuzhaigou Valley

CO.description: The best-preserved colonial city in South America, protected by massive fortifications built by Spain to guard silver shipments.
CO.name: Port, Fortresses and Group of Monuments, Cartagena

CO.description: A biological corridor connecting South and North America, with extraordinary biodiversity in lowland forests and swamps.
CO.name: Los Katíos National Park

CO.description: The Colombian Eje Cafetero — a 100-year-old tradition of shade-grown coffee on steep Andean slopes, shaping culture and identity.
CO.name: Coffee Cultural Landscape of Colombia

CU.description: A living museum of baroque and neoclassical architecture, with the largest fortification in the Americas at El Morro castle.
CU.name: Old Havana and its Fortification System

CU.description: A perfectly preserved colonial Spanish town with pastel houses and cobblestone streets, surrounded by sugar mill ruins.
CU.name: Trinidad and the Valley de los Ingenios

CU.description: Dramatic limestone mogotes (hills) rise from a fertile valley where tobacco for Cuban cigars is grown using traditional methods.
CU.name: Viñales Valley

CZ.description: One of the best-preserved medieval capitals in Europe, with the Charles Bridge, Hradčany Castle, and Old Town Square.
CZ.name: Historic Centre of Prague

CZ.description: A Bohemian town frozen in time, with a magnificent castle winding along the Vltava River.
CZ.name: Historic Centre of Český Krumlov

CZ.description: A silver-mining city that was once one of Europe's wealthiest, featuring the Ossuary (Bone Church) decorated with human bones.
CZ.name: Kutná Hora: Historical Town Centre with the Church of Saint Barbara

DE.description: The largest Gothic cathedral in Northern Europe, under construction for over 600 years (1248–1880), dominating Cologne's skyline.
DE.name: Cologne Cathedral

DE.description: One of the first UNESCO sites, Charlemagne's Palace Chapel (792–805 AD) became the model for Carolingian architecture across Europe.
DE.name: Aachen Cathedral

DE.description: The crown jewel is Sanssouci Palace, Frederick the Great's rococo summer residence and private retreat.
DE.name: Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin

DE.description: A remarkably preserved medieval town that influenced the development of art and architecture in Central Europe.
DE.name: Town of Bamberg

DK.description: A 10th-century Viking complex considered 'Denmark's birth certificate' — where King Harald Bluetooth converted Denmark to Christianity.
DK.name: Jelling Mounds, Runic Stones and Church

DK.description: The first Gothic cathedral in Scandinavia and burial site of 39 Danish kings and queens since 1559.
DK.name: Roskilde Cathedral

DK.description: The castle that inspired Elsinore in Shakespeare's Hamlet, guarding the narrow strait between Denmark and Sweden.
DK.name: Kronborg Castle

DO.description: The first European city in the Americas, founded in 1498 by Bartholomew Columbus, with the oldest cathedral, university, and hospital in the New World.
DO.name: Colonial City of Santo Domingo

EG.description: The Great Pyramid of Giza — the only surviving Wonder of the Ancient World — along with the Great Sphinx and Step Pyramid.
EG.name: Memphis and its Necropolis – the Pyramid Fields

EG.description: Ramesses II's twin temples, relocated block-by-block in the 1960s to save them from the rising waters of Lake Nasser.
EG.name: Nubian Monuments from Abu Simbel to Philae

EG.description: One of the world's oldest Islamic cities, with 600 mosques, madrasahs, mausoleums, and fountains from the 7th century onward.
EG.name: Islamic Cairo

EG.description: The Valley of the Kings — burial ground of pharaohs including Tutankhamun — and the Karnak temple complex.
EG.name: Ancient Thebes with its Necropolis

ES.description: The masterpiece of Moorish architecture: the Alhambra palace complex with its intricate geometric decoration and gardens.
ES.name: Alhambra, Generalife and Albayzín, Granada

ES.description: Seven architectural works by Gaudí including the Sagrada Família, Park Güell, and Casa Milà — visionary examples of organic Art Nouveau.
ES.name: Works of Antoni Gaudí

ES.description: The endpoint of the famous Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route, centered on the cathedral said to contain the tomb of St. James.
ES.name: Santiago de Compostela (Old Town)

ES.description: A city of three cultures — Christian, Muslim, and Jewish — that coexisted for centuries, creating remarkable architectural harmony.
ES.name: Historic City of Toledo

ET.description: Eleven monolithic 12th-century churches carved underground from a single rock — considered 'the eighth wonder of the world' and a living pilgrimage site.
ET.name: Rock-Hewn Churches, Lalibela

ET.description: Ancient obelisks (stelae) mark the tombs of the Aksumite kingdom (1st–13th centuries AD) — one of the great civilizations of antiquity.
ET.name: Aksum

ET.description: The 17th-century royal enclosure of Gondar contains six castles, earning Ethiopia the nickname 'Camelot of Africa.'
ET.name: Fasil Ghebbi, Gondar Region

ET.description: A dramatic highland plateau with cliffs dropping 1,500 m, home to the gelada baboon and the endangered Ethiopian wolf.
ET.name: Simien National Park

FI.description: An 18th-century sea fortress built on six islands protecting Helsinki harbour — today a residential area with 800 inhabitants.
FI.name: Fortress of Suomenlinna

FI.description: One of the oldest and best-preserved wooden towns in Scandinavia, with 600 buildings from the 18th and 19th centuries.
FI.name: Old Rauma

FI.description: A Lutheran log church from 1763, a masterpiece of Finnish carpenter craftsmanship combining Gothic and Renaissance elements.
FI.name: Petäjävesi Old Church

FR.description: The grandest example of French classical architecture: Louis XIV's palace with 700 rooms and 800 hectares of formal gardens.
FR.name: Palace and Park of Versailles

FR.description: A rocky tidal island crowned by a medieval monastery, connected to the mainland only by sand at low tide — one of France's most iconic landmarks.
FR.name: Mont-Saint-Michel and its Bay

FR.description: The best-preserved medieval cathedral in France, famous for its stunning Gothic architecture and 176 stained-glass windows.
FR.name: Chartres Cathedral

FR.description: From the Eiffel Tower to the Louvre, the banks of the Seine embody the history of Paris across 2,000 years.
FR.name: Banks of the Seine in Paris

FR.description: The world's greatest collection of prehistoric art, including the Lascaux cave paintings dating back 17,000 years.
FR.name: Prehistoric Sites and Decorated Caves of the Vézère Valley

GB.description: The world's most famous prehistoric megalithic monument, with massive standing stones aligned to the summer solstice.
GB.name: Stonehenge, Avebury and Associated Sites

GB.description: A millennium-old fortress, palace, and prison housing the Crown Jewels — with Beefeaters guarding its traditions since 1485.
GB.name: Tower of London

GB.description: The Palace of Westminster (Parliament) and Westminster Abbey are two of England's most iconic monuments.
GB.name: Westminster Palace, Westminster Abbey and Saint Margaret's Church

GB.description: The cradle of English Christianity, where the murder of Archbishop Thomas Becket in 1170 sparked one of history's greatest pilgrimages.
GB.name: Canterbury Cathedral, St Augustine's Abbey and St Martin's Church

GB.description: Built around natural hot springs, Bath features Britain's most celebrated Roman baths and perfectly preserved Georgian architecture.
GB.name: City of Bath

GB.description: Birthplace of the Industrial Revolution — the world's first cast-iron bridge (1779) stands over the Severn Gorge.
GB.name: Ironbridge Gorge

GH.description: A chain of European-built forts along Ghana's coast that were used as dungeons for millions of enslaved Africans.
GH.name: Forts and Castles, Volta, Greater Accra, Central and Western Regions

GH.description: The remaining sacred buildings of the Asante people — formerly the richest kingdom in West Africa.
GH.name: Asante Traditional Buildings

GR.description: The Parthenon and other monuments on this rocky outcrop are the supreme expression of the ancient Greek genius.
GR.name: Acropolis, Athens

GR.description: The sanctuary of Apollo where the famous Oracle pronounced prophecies, considered the 'navel of the world' by ancient Greeks.
GR.name: Delphi

GR.description: The birthplace of medicine, featuring the best-preserved ancient Greek theater with perfect acoustics.
GR.name: Sanctuary of Asklepios at Epidaurus

GR.description: The sacred grove and sanctuary where the Olympic Games were held every four years for over a millennium.
GR.name: Archaeological Site of Olympia

GR.description: Byzantine monasteries perched atop extraordinary sandstone pillars rising 400 meters from the plain of Thessaly.
GR.name: Meteora

HU.description: The twin cities of Buda (Buda Castle) and Pest (Parliament Building) frame the Danube in a spectacular urban ensemble.
HU.name: Budapest, with the Banks of the Danube

HU.description: A preserved example of traditional rural life in the Cserhát hills, with a 13th-century castle and folk architecture.
HU.name: Hollókő Old Village and its Surroundings

HU.description: Europe's largest semi-arid steppe with ancient pastoral traditions still practiced by Hungarian csikós cowboys.
HU.name: Hortobágy National Park — the Puszta

ID.description: The world's largest Buddhist temple (9th century) features 2,672 relief panels and 504 Buddha statues on a terraced pyramid.
ID.name: Borobudur Temple Compounds

ID.description: The largest Hindu temple compound in Indonesia (9th century), dedicated to the Trimurti of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.
ID.name: Prambanan Temple Compounds

ID.description: Home to the Komodo dragon — the world's largest living lizard — and spectacular marine biodiversity.
ID.name: Komodo National Park

ID.description: One of the world's most important prehistoric sites, where over 50 Homo erectus fossils have been found.
ID.name: Sangiran Early Man Site

IN.description: The white-marble mausoleum built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan for his wife Mumtaz Mahal — 'a teardrop on the cheek of time.'
IN.name: Taj Mahal

IN.description: The main residence of the Mughal emperors until 1638, this red sandstone fort contains palaces, mosques, and halls.
IN.name: Agra Fort

IN.description: Thirty rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments containing paintings and sculptures considered masterpieces of Buddhist religious art.
IN.name: Ajanta Caves

IN.description: 34 caves carved between the 6th and 11th centuries AD, representing Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain art side by side.
IN.name: Ellora Caves

IN.description: The highest brick minaret in the world (72.5 m), built in the 12th century at the onset of Islamic rule in India.
IN.name: Qutb Minar and its Monuments

IN.description: Home to two-thirds of the world's one-horned rhinoceroses, along with tigers, elephants, and wild water buffalo.
IN.name: Kaziranga National Park

IN.description: The site where Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree — one of the most sacred Buddhist sites.
IN.name: Mahabodhi Temple Complex, Bodh Gaya

IR.description: The ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire (6th–4th centuries BCE), featuring massive terrace complexes and bas-relief carvings.
IR.name: Persepolis

IR.description: One of the largest city squares in the world (512 × 163 m), surrounded by the Shah Mosque, Ali Qapu Palace, and bazaars.
IR.name: Meidan Emam (Naqsh-e Jahan Square), Esfahan

IR.description: The first dynasty capital of the Achaemenid Empire, containing the tomb of Cyrus the Great — the founder of human rights.
IR.name: Pasargadae

IR.description: The royal Qajar complex in Tehran (18th–19th centuries), combining Persian craftsmanship with European influences.
IR.name: Golestan Palace

IT.description: The Eternal City encompasses the Colosseum, the Roman Forum, the Pantheon, and 2,700 years of architectural history.
IT.name: Historic Centre of Rome

IT.description: Built on 118 islands separated by canals, Venice is a unique masterpiece of art, architecture, and an extraordinary relationship with the sea.
IT.name: Venice and its Lagoon

IT.description: The cradle of the Renaissance, home to the Cathedral (Duomo), Uffizi Gallery, and works of Botticelli, Michelangelo, and da Vinci.
IT.name: Historic Centre of Florence

IT.description: Preserved by the 79 AD eruption of Vesuvius, these cities provide an unparalleled snapshot of ancient Roman life.
IT.name: Archaeological Areas of Pompeii, Herculaneum, and Torre Annunziata

IT.description: A dramatic coastline with vertically stratified settlements, gardens, and citrus groves clinging to precipitous cliffs above the Mediterranean.
IT.name: Amalfi Coast

IT.description: Five dramatic clifftop villages linked by ancient terraced vineyards, olive groves, and coastal paths along the Italian Riviera.
IT.name: Cinque Terre

JO.description: The ancient Nabataean capital carved entirely from rose-red sandstone cliffs, known as 'the Rose City.' One of the New Seven Wonders.
JO.name: Petra

JO.description: A dramatic desert landscape of sandstone mountains and canyons with petroglyphs spanning 12,000 years of human history.
JO.name: Wadi Rum Protected Area

JP.description: The oldest surviving wooden structures in the world, containing some of the finest examples of Buddhist art from the 7th century.
JP.name: Buddhist Monuments in the Horyu-ji Area

JP.description: Seventeen historic monuments including Kinkaku-ji (the Golden Pavilion) and Ginkaku-ji, representing 1,000 years as Japan's imperial capital.
JP.name: Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto

JP.description: Includes Tōdai-ji temple with its Great Buddha (Daibutsu), one of Japan's most celebrated cultural landmarks.
JP.name: Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara

JP.description: The lavishly decorated Tōshō-gū mausoleum and Rinnō-ji temple complex in the mountains north of Tokyo.
JP.name: Shrines and Temples of Nikkō

JP.description: The skeletal ruins of the Prefectural Industrial Promotion Hall, the only structure to survive the 1945 atomic bomb explosion.
JP.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial (Genbaku Dome)

JP.description: A Shinto shrine on Miyajima Island with a famous floating torii gate — one of Japan's three most celebrated views.
JP.name: Itsukushima Shinto Shrine

JP.description: Japan's iconic 3,776-meter volcano has inspired Japanese art and poetry for centuries, attracting 300,000 climbers annually.
JP.name: Fujisan (Mount Fuji)

KE.description: The world's largest desert lake and oldest lake in East Africa, a cradle of human evolution with Homo habilis fossils.
KE.name: Lake Turkana National Parks

KE.description: Africa's second-highest peak (5,199 m) is a major water tower of eastern Africa, with unique afro-alpine flora.
KE.name: Mount Kenya National Park / Natural Forest

KE.description: The oldest and best-preserved Swahili settlement in East Africa, built without mortar — surviving buildings date to the 14th century.
KE.name: Lamu Old Town

KE.description: 11 forest sites that contain the remains of villages of the Mijikenda people, sacred centers of cultural and spiritual life.
KE.name: Sacred Mijikenda Kaya Forests

KH.description: The Khmer Empire capital (9th–15th centuries) contains the world's largest religious monument — Angkor Wat — spread over 400 km².
KH.name: Angkor

LB.description: A unique Umayyad city from the early 8th century, providing exceptional evidence of Islamic urban planning.
LB.name: Anjar

LB.description: Home to the best-preserved Roman temples in the world, including the massive Temple of Jupiter with 20-meter columns.
LB.name: Baalbek

LB.description: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, where the alphabet was developed and exported by Phoenician traders.
LB.name: Byblos

LB.description: The ancient Phoenician metropolis that invented purple dye, established Carthage, and first used glass in trade.
LB.name: Tyre

LK.description: A 5th-century rock fortress and palace ruin rising 200 m from the jungle floor, with stunning frescoes and water gardens.
LK.name: Ancient City of Sigiriya

LK.description: The ancient capital of Sri Lanka for over 1,000 years contains some of the world's oldest surviving Buddhist monuments.
LK.name: Sacred City of Anuradhapura

LK.description: A historic port city built by Dutch colonists in the 17th century, illustrating the interaction between European architecture and South Asian tradition.
LK.name: Old Town of Galle and its Fortifications

LK.description: The last capital of the ancient kingdom, home to the Temple of the Tooth Relic — the most revered Buddhist shrine in Sri Lanka.
LK.name: Sacred City of Kandy

LY.description: The best-preserved Roman city in the world, birthplace of Emperor Septimius Severus — with a 25,000-seat theater and magnificent Arch of Septimius.
LY.name: Archaeological Site of Leptis Magna

LY.description: The ancient Greek city founded in 631 BCE features a sanctuary of Apollo and the Temple of Zeus, larger than the Parthenon.
LY.name: Archaeological Site of Cyrene

LY.description: Thousands of cave paintings spanning 12,000 years in the Sahara Desert, depicting wildlife that disappeared as the desert expanded.
LY.name: Rock-Art Sites of Tadrart Acacus

MA.description: The world's largest intact medieval city, with 9,000 alleys and no cars — founded in 789 CE, home to the world's oldest university.
MA.name: Medina of Fez

MA.description: A living medieval city centered on the Djemaa el-Fna square — one of the world's great public spaces.
MA.name: Medina of Marrakesh

MA.description: A spectacular earthen fortified village (ksar) on the former caravan route, used as backdrop for dozens of films.
MA.name: Ksar of Aït-Ben-Haddou

MA.description: The best-preserved Roman ruins in Morocco, featuring remarkable floor mosaics from the 3rd century AD.
MA.name: Archaeological Site of Volubilis

ML.description: The Great Mosque of Djenné — the largest mud-brick building in the world — rebuilt annually by the entire community.
ML.name: Old Towns of Djenné

ML.description: Once 'the city of gold,' Timbuktu was a center of Islamic learning with 180 Quranic schools and 25,000 students in the 15th century.
ML.name: Timbuktu

MN.description: The heartland of nomadic empires for millennia, from the first Turks to Genghis Khan, featuring the ruins of the Mongol capital Karakorum.
MN.name: Orkhon Valley Cultural Landscape

MX.description: The largest city in pre-Columbian Americas, featuring the Pyramid of the Sun (third-largest pyramid on Earth) and Avenue of the Dead.
MX.name: Pre-Hispanic City of Teotihuacan

MX.description: The Mayan city where El Castillo pyramid's shadow creates a serpent effect during equinoxes — one of the New Seven Wonders.
MX.name: Pre-Hispanic City of Chichen-Itza

MX.description: The most artistically refined Maya city, with the Palace and Temple of the Inscriptions containing the tomb of King Pakal.
MX.name: Pre-Hispanic City and National Park of Palenque

MX.description: The first major Mesoamerican city, capital of the Zapotec civilization from 500 BCE to 700 CE.
MX.name: Historic Centre of Oaxaca and Archaeological Zone of Monte Albán

MY.description: Historic cities of the Straits of Malacca that demonstrate multi-cultural trading ports shaped by successive colonial powers.
MY.name: Melaka and George Town

MY.description: Mount Kinabalu (4,095 m) in Sabah hosts one of the world's richest assemblages of plants, including 800 orchid species.
MY.name: Kinabalu Park

MY.description: Features the world's largest cave passage, the Sarawak Chamber, and some of the most extraordinary examples of karst topography.
MY.name: Gunung Mulu National Park

NG.description: The last sacred forest in Yorubaland, with shrines, sculptures, and the Oshun river goddess — a living tradition of supernatural beliefs.
NG.name: Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove

NG.description: A remarkable cultural landscape with a palace, terraced fields, and ironworking traditions in the Mandara Mountains.
NG.name: Sukur Cultural Landscape

NL.description: The world's largest concentration of windmills (19) — built in the 18th century to manage water levels in the Dutch polders.
NL.name: Mill Network at Kinderdijk-Elshout

NL.description: An ancient island reclaimed from the sea, demonstrating humanity's centuries-long struggle with water management.
NL.name: Schokland and Surroundings

NL.description: A 135-km ring of fortifications around Amsterdam (1883–1920), protecting the city using a unique system of controlled flooding.
NL.name: Amsterdam Defence Line

NO.description: Colorful wooden Hanseatic League buildings from the 14th–16th centuries — once a major trading center for dried fish.
NO.name: Bryggen (The Wharf) in Bergen

NO.description: The oldest stave church in Norway (12th century), featuring intricate Viking carved ornamentation.
NO.name: Urnes Stave Church

NO.description: Over 6,000 carvings of animals, boats, and humans carved into rock 2,000–7,000 years ago, painted red-ochre on a fjord.
NO.name: Rock Art of Alta

NO.description: The most spectacular fjords in the world, with vertical cliff walls rising 1,400 m from the water.
NO.name: West Norwegian Fjords — Geirangerfjord and Nærøyfjord

NP.description: Home to Mount Everest (8,849 m), the world's highest peak, along with glaciers, deep gorges, and the Sherpa culture.
NP.name: Sagarmatha National Park

NP.description: One of Asia's finest wildlife reserves, protecting the last populations of the one-horned rhinoceros and the Bengal tiger in Nepal.
NP.name: Chitwan National Park

NP.description: Seven monument zones including Pashupatinath Temple, Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), and Boudhanath stupa.
NP.name: Kathmandu Valley

NP.description: The sacred garden where Queen Mayadevi gave birth to Siddhartha Gautama (Buddha) in 623 BCE.
NP.name: Lumbini, the Birthplace of the Lord Buddha

NZ.description: A vast wilderness of fjords, glaciers, and mountains — the last landmass to be settled by humans (Māori in 1200 AD).
NZ.name: Te Wahipounamu – South West New Zealand

NZ.description: New Zealand's oldest national park, with active volcanoes sacred to the Māori — Mount Ngauruhoe doubled as Mount Doom in Lord of the Rings.
NZ.name: Tongariro National Park

NZ.description: Five remote island groups representing some of the Earth's most diverse and abundant concentration of seabirds and penguins.
NZ.name: New Zealand Sub-Antarctic Islands

PE.description: The 15th-century Inca citadel perched 2,430 m above the Sacred Valley, 'discovered' by Hiram Bingham in 1911 — one of the New Seven Wonders.
PE.name: Historic Sanctuary of Machu Picchu

PE.description: Capital of the Chimu Kingdom (9th–15th centuries), the largest pre-Columbian city in South America.
PE.name: Chan Chan Archaeological Zone

PE.description: Home to the world's highest tropical mountain range, with 663 glaciers and rare wildlife including the spectacled bear.
PE.name: Huascarán National Park

PH.description: The 2,000-year-old Ifugao rice terraces carved into the mountains of Luzon, often called 'the eighth wonder of the world.'
PH.name: Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras

PH.description: Four churches built by the Spanish in the 16th–18th centuries, representing a unique blend of European Baroque and Asian architectural styles.
PH.name: Baroque Churches of the Philippines

PH.description: Features a spectacular limestone karst landscape with an underground river 8.2 km long — one of the longest in the world.
PH.name: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park

PH.description: A pristine coral reef in the Sulu Sea, the marine equivalent of a rainforest with 600 fish species and 360 coral species.
PH.name: Tubbataha Reef Marine Park

PK.description: One of the world's earliest cities (2500 BCE), part of the Indus Valley Civilization with sophisticated urban planning.
PK.name: Archaeological Ruins at Moenjodaro

PK.description: The Lahore Fort contains 21 monuments from the Mughal era; the Shalamar Gardens represent the height of Mughal garden design.
PK.name: Fort and Shalamar Gardens in Lahore

PK.description: An important city at the crossroads of three trade routes, Taxila was a center of Gandhara culture and Buddhist learning from the 5th century BCE.
PK.name: Taxila

PK.description: An outstanding example of early Muslim military architecture in South Asia, built by Sher Shah Suri in the 16th century.
PK.name: Rohtas Fort

PL.description: One of the first UNESCO sites, Kraków's medieval core with its magnificent market square is remarkably well-preserved.
PL.name: Historic Centre of Kraków

PL.description: Underground cathedral, chapels, and lakes entirely carved from salt — operated continuously for 700 years.
PL.name: Wieliczka and Bochnia Royal Salt Mines

PL.description: A monument to the murder of over 1.1 million people, primarily Jews — the largest extermination camp of the Holocaust.
PL.name: Auschwitz Birkenau — German Nazi Concentration and Extermination Camp

PL.description: The last primeval forest of Europe, home to the European bison (żubr), the continent's heaviest land animal.
PL.name: Białowieża Forest

PT.description: The first European colonial town in the Atlantic (14th century), an important waystation for explorers sailing to the New World.
PT.name: Central Zone of the Town of Angra do Heroísmo in the Azores

PT.description: Manueline-style monuments built to celebrate Vasco da Gama's voyage to India, at the point where the Tagus meets the Atlantic.
PT.name: Monastery of the Hieronymites and Tower of Belém

PT.description: A 19th-century Romantic architectural ensemble in a mountain setting, featuring the colorful Pena Palace.
PT.name: Historic Centre of Sintra

PT.description: The oldest demarcated wine region in the world (1756), producing Port wine from terraced vineyards along the Douro River.
PT.name: Alto Douro Wine Region

RU.description: Peter the Great's window to Europe, with the Hermitage, Winter Palace, Peterhof fountains, and 18th-century architectural masterpieces.
RU.name: Historic Centre of Saint Petersburg and Related Groups of Monuments

RU.description: The Kremlin's cathedrals and palaces sit beside Red Square's St. Basil's Cathedral — the symbol of Russia's power and history.
RU.name: Moscow Kremlin and Red Square

RU.description: The world's deepest lake (1,642 m), containing 20% of all unfrozen fresh water on Earth — with 3,700 unique plant and animal species.
RU.name: Lake Baikal

RU.description: The most outstanding example of active volcanism in the world: 29 active volcanoes and the world's greatest concentration of geysers.
RU.name: Volcanoes of Kamchatka

RU.description: The source of major Siberian rivers, with mountain steppe, taiga, and glaciers supporting snow leopards and Altai argali sheep.
RU.name: Golden Mountains of Altai

SA.description: Saudi Arabia's first UNESCO site: a Nabataean city from the 1st century BCE with 111 rock-cut monumental tombs.
SA.name: Al-Hijr Archaeological Site (Madâin Sâlih)

SA.description: The first capital of the Saudi dynasty, founded in the 15th century in the Najd region.
SA.name: At-Turaif District in ad-Dir'iyah

SA.description: A trading port since the 7th century, featuring remarkable coral buildings and the old Jeddah Corniche.
SA.name: Historic Jeddah, the Gate to Makkah

SE.description: The private residence of the Swedish royal family, with a 17th-century palace and perfectly preserved Baroque theater.
SE.name: Royal Domain of Drottningholm

SE.description: The 8th–10th century Viking trading center on Lake Mälaren — Sweden's first town and a crossroads of trade routes.
SE.name: Birka and Hovgården

SE.description: Seven 19th-century timber farmhouses with painted rooms, representing the peak of traditional Swedish folk art.
SE.name: Decorated Farmhouses of Hälsingland

SN.description: The small island off Dakar was the largest slave-trading center on the African coast — a sobering memorial to the transatlantic trade.
SN.name: Island of Gorée

SN.description: Inhabited for over 1,000 years by the Bassari people, preserving rice cultivation and cultural traditions unchanged for centuries.
SN.name: Bassari Country: Bassari, Fula and Bedik Cultural Landscapes

TH.description: Ruins of the Thai capital (1350–1767) that was one of the world's largest cities, with 14 km of city walls and hundreds of temples.
TH.name: Historic City of Ayutthaya

TH.description: The first capital of the Thai Kingdom (13th–14th centuries), with magnificent temples and sculptures in a distinctive Thai style.
TH.name: Historic Town of Sukhothai and Associated Towns

TH.description: One of the largest intact forest areas in mainland Southeast Asia, supporting tigers, elephants, gaur, and banteng.
TH.name: Thungyai-Huai Kha Khaeng Wildlife Sanctuaries

TN.description: One of the finest medinas in the Arab-Muslim world, with 700 historic buildings and the Ez-Zitouna Mosque as its heart.
TN.name: Medina of Tunis

TN.description: The ancient Phoenician and Roman city defeated by Rome in the Punic Wars — its founding myths include the story of Queen Dido.
TN.name: Archaeological Site of Carthage

TN.description: The third-largest Roman amphitheater in the world (35,000 capacity), better preserved than the Colosseum in Rome.
TN.name: Amphitheatre of El Jem

TR.description: The Hagia Sophia, Topkapi Palace, and the Blue Mosque at the crossroads of Europe and Asia — 2,600 years of layered civilizations.
TR.name: Historic Areas of Istanbul

TR.description: A surreal volcanic landscape with fairy chimneys, underground cities housing up to 20,000 people, and rock-cut churches with Byzantine frescoes.
TR.name: Göreme National Park and the Rock Sites of Cappadocia

TR.description: Nine distinct layers of the legendary city of the Trojan War, first excavated by Heinrich Schliemann in 1870.
TR.name: Troy

TR.description: Sparkling white terraces of calcium carbonate (travertine) formed by thermal springs, alongside a Greco-Roman spa city.
TR.name: Hierapolis-Pamukkale

TZ.description: The world's largest intact volcanic caldera hosts the greatest density of large mammals on Earth: lions, elephants, and black rhinos.
TZ.name: Ngorongoro Conservation Area

TZ.description: Home to the greatest wildlife spectacle on Earth — the annual wildebeest migration of 1.5 million animals.
TZ.name: Serengeti National Park

TZ.description: Remains of East African trading ports from the 9th to 19th centuries that controlled the gold trade from Zimbabwe.
TZ.name: Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Ruins of Songo Mnara

TZ.description: A Swahili, Arab, Persian, Indian, and European trading city, center of the Indian Ocean trade and the spice trade.
TZ.name: Stone Town of Zanzibar

UA.description: Founded in the 11th century by Yaroslav the Wise, the cathedral contains original Byzantine mosaics and frescoes.
UA.name: Saint-Sophia Cathedral and Related Monastic Buildings, Kyiv

UA.description: A network of underground tunnels and catacombs beneath the monastery hold the mummified remains of monks and saints.
UA.name: Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra (Monastery of the Caves)

US.description: The Colorado River carved this 446-km gorge reaching 1.6 km deep over 5-6 million years, exposing 2 billion years of geological history.
US.name: Grand Canyon National Park

US.description: The world's first national park contains half the world's geysers, including Old Faithful, above one of Earth's largest supervolcanoes.
US.name: Yellowstone National Park

US.description: Iconic granite monoliths El Capitan and Half Dome rise above a valley carved by glaciers 10,000 years ago.
US.name: Yosemite National Park

US.description: France's gift to America (1886) — the copper lady at the gateway to New York Harbor has welcomed millions of immigrants.
US.name: Statue of Liberty

US.description: The largest subtropical wilderness in the US, a 'river of grass' that is the only place where alligators and crocodiles coexist.
US.name: Everglades National Park

US.description: A 3,700-year-old mound complex in Louisiana built by a hunter-gatherer society with no agriculture.
US.name: Monumental Earthworks of Poverty Point

UZ.description: The walled inner town of Khiva, an ancient oasis city on the Silk Road, preserved as a living museum of Islamic architecture.
UZ.name: Itchan Kala

UZ.description: A 2,500-year-old city and major center of Islamic scholarship, featuring the Ark citadel, Kalyan Minaret, and countless madrasahs.
UZ.name: Historic Centre of Bukhara

UZ.description: Founded in the 7th century BCE and Tamerlane's capital, featuring the Registan — perhaps the most beautiful urban ensemble in Central Asia.
UZ.name: Samarkand – Crossroads of Cultures

VN.description: Over 1,600 limestone islands and islets rising from emerald waters in the Gulf of Tonkin, creating a seascape of extraordinary beauty.
VN.name: Hạ Long Bay

VN.description: The imperial city of the Nguyễn dynasty (1802–1945) featuring the Citadel, Royal Palace, temples, and royal tombs along the Perfume River.
VN.name: Complex of Huế Monuments

VN.description: An exceptionally well-preserved Southeast Asian trading port from the 2nd century BC, reflecting cultural traditions from many civilizations.
VN.name: Hội An Ancient Town

VN.description: A remarkable collection of tower temples built by Cham kings between the 4th and 14th centuries.
VN.name: Mỹ Sơn Sanctuary

ZA.description: Where Nelson Mandela was imprisoned for 18 of his 27 years — now a symbol of the triumph of the human spirit over injustice.
ZA.name: Robben Island

ZA.description: The Sterkfontein and surrounding caves have yielded more than a third of all early hominid fossils ever found.
ZA.name: Fossil Hominid Sites of South Africa (Cradle of Humankind)

ZA.description: Africa's largest estuarine system, where hippos and crocodiles coexist with humpback whale breeding grounds offshore.
ZA.name: Greater St Lucia Wetland Park (iSimangaliso)

ZA.description: One of the world's six floral kingdoms, with 9,600 plant species in an area smaller than Portugal.
ZA.name: Cape Floral Region Protected Areas

ZW.description: The world's largest curtain of falling water: 1,708 m wide and 108 m tall — called 'the smoke that thunders' in Kololo.
ZW.name: Mosi-oa-Tunya / Victoria Falls

ZW.description: The ruins of a medieval stone city (11th–15th centuries), capital of the Kingdom of Zimbabwe — the largest ancient structure south of the Sahara.
ZW.name: Great Zimbabwe National Monument

ZW.description: The capital of the Torwa dynasty (1450–1683), built using a distinctive terrace and platform construction technique.
ZW.name: Khami Ruins National Monument
